title.narrative: Exploring scale-up opportunities for increased access to safe drinking water

description.narrative:
In spite of the efforts of government and NGOs, there remains a disparity in respect of coverage in the supply of potable water especially in coastal areas. Due to lack of access to safe drinking water, water borne diseases remain a major problem. A number of factors i.e. a) high population density; b) high levels of arsenic in the groundwater; and c) high microbial contamination levels in the surface water, work as impediments to safe water supply. Saline water intrusion; drainage congestion; extreme events; and changes in coastal morphology have been identified as primary physical effects for the vulnerabilities in the coastal areas of Bangladesh.
To overcome the situation, CAFOD and Caritas Switzerland have supported Caritas Bangladesh in the implementation of WASH projects in the south of Bangladesh. CAFOD have supported work through DfID Match Fund 1 (BAN157 and BAN158) and Caritas Switzerland have supported a project with the overall objective of the project to 'provide access to safe drinking water for 4,000 disadvantaged families'. This project introduced chlorination technology for water purification through the training of 19 experts. These projects have been running parallel and have both been implemented by Caritas Bangladesh.
The mid-term review for Match Fund 1 (see BAN157) revealed some positive findings in relation to the chlorination/water purification technology introduced by the project, which suggests potential scope to scale-up this intervention in the future. CAFOD in partnership with Caritas Switzerland and Caritas Bangladesh have agreed to support the undertaking of a feasibility study of this technology, to understand if and how it can be scaled-up. Providing the feasibility study is positive, a business plan will be developed so this work can be taken forward in the future.
